projectDesc.p: Transliteration is ISO-15919 with ṟ (ಱ) and ḻ (ೞ) kept apart from r and ḷ, and e/o short, ē/ō long; vocalic r is r̥ (Gai prints ṛ). Capital letters of the print are lower-cased in the text of the inscriptions. Anusvāra is kept as printed (ṁ), also before stops (the other texts of the project write the class nasal). Headings (head) keep Gai's romanization and capitals.

Structure: group of text, one per inscription (n = its serial number; the numbers printed are in the head; Nos. 26 and 47-50 have none in the print), inside group type="century". head = the reference, number, date and place printed above the text. lb n = the line number printed at the left margin; lb break="no" follows a line that ends in a hyphen (the hyphen of the print is kept: it may divide a word or a compound). pb n = the page number of the print.

Word junctions: Gai writes "=" between two words that are written together on the stone (sandhi). Here "x = y" becomes "x y" when y begins with a vowel (its vowel is part of the preceding letter) or when x ends in a consonant and y begins with a consonant. A vowel-initial word that is not so joined is written with "°" before the vowel, also a vowel-initial member of a compound after a hyphen when the letter before the hyphen is a vowel (śrī-°akālavarṣa). Two words, the first ending in a consonant and the second beginning with one, that are not joined are separated by "·" (a middle dot, without spaces). A "=" in any other position is kept as printed.

Editorial interventions of the print: (1) parentheses in the Kannada text, kept as printed until each has been classified (gai_parens.py): choice resp="#GSG" with orig and reg for a correction, unclear resp="#GSG" for an addition or an unclear letter; (2) the footnotes, to be encoded as app with rdg source="#RICE" or "#FLEET"; until then each is kept in an XML comment at the place of its mark. Notes of the editor in English ("Skt. verse.", "(Other side)", "etc." ...) are note type="editorial" xml:lang="en". Square brackets, asterisks, dots for lacunae, the bars | and || and the metrical signs are as printed.
